case_title: Mahavir Singh v. State of Haryana
previous_criminal_record: Not stated (respondent referred to an earlier criminal case between the parties; the judgment does not record a criminal record for the appellant)
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: grudge over the deceased's marriage to the wife and an earlier assault incident between them
weapon: Hexa blade and frame of an Aari (saw) found with blood; the murder weapon is not expressly identified
evidence_type: Circumstantial (last seen together, chain of circumstances), medical evidence, recovery of clothes and articles on disclosure statements, oral testimony
confession: No confession described; disclosure statements of the appellant and co-accused led to recoveries, which the courts relied on
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302, 120B and 201; life imprisonment and Rs.5,000 fine (s.302/120B); two years RI and Rs.1,000 fine (s.201), with six months RI in default of fine on s.201
high_court_outcome: Criminal appeal dismissed on 20.1.2010; conviction and sentence upheld
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302); criminal conspiracy (IPC s.120B); causing disappearance of evidence (IPC s.201)
neutral_facts: The victim was reported missing around 21 June 1995, and his body was later found floating in a canal, after a chappal was recovered on a path leading to the canal near a bridge. The victim's brother, who had gone searching on a motorcycle, reported seeing a chappal, a saw, two pieces of blade, blood and pieces of meat on the path and the body on the water's surface. A missing-person report was made by the victim's mother, and a first information report was later registered. The prosecution case was that the accused and a co-accused killed the victim on the intervening night of 21/22 June 1995 at the instigation of the victim's wife, with whom the co-accused was alleged to have an illicit relationship, and that the body was thrown into the canal. The accused was alleged to have a grudge over the victim's marriage to the wife and a previous fight with the victim. A family member testified that the victim had been seen with the accused and the co-accused on 21 June 1995. A doctor testified that the victim had been murdered about one week before the post-mortem, which found grievous injuries to the neck and scalp and multiple skull fractures. Recoveries were made on the disclosure statements of the accused and the co-accused: the victim's chappal, and blood-stained shirt and trousers of the accused found in a polythene bag under a bridge. Further blood-stained clothing was recovered hidden near the village. The laboratory reported human blood on the clothes, and blood was also found on a hexa blade and the frame of a saw.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; grievous injuries to neck and scalp; multiple skull fractures
premeditation_planning: Not stated; conspiracy was alleged by the investigation and the s.120B conviction was upheld, but no separate finding on planning is recorded
motive: alleged: grudge over the deceased's marriage to the wife, an earlier assault, and the co-accused's alleged illicit relationship with the wife
key_evidence_accepted: Last-seen evidence (PW6, and PW8/PW9 on what PW9 reported); medical opinion (PW1) that death occurred about a week before post-mortem; medical injury findings; recoveries of chappal and blood-stained clothing with FSL report of human blood
witness_credibility: Court found discrepancies in inquest report and depositions to be minor; defence had not cross-examined the Investigating Officer or ASI on them, and the court relied on the witnesses' evidence
post_offence_conduct: Blood-stained clothes concealed near the village were recovered on the appellant's own disclosure statement; the appellant gave no explanation for the deceased's whereabouts in his s.313 statement
trial_duration: offence: 21.6.1995/22.6.1995; trial judgment: 4.9.2001/7.9.2001; High Court: 20.1.2010; Supreme Court: 23.5.2014
legal_representation: Appellant: Sanjay Sharawat, Balraj S. Malik; State of Haryana (respondent): Nupur Choudhary, Samir Ali Khan, Sanjay Jain
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; chargesheet filed; trial completed in Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302, 120B, 201 IPC, life imprisonment; High Court (20.1.2010): appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence upheld; Supreme Court (23.5.2014): appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Sufficient motive existed; no question on independent witnesses was put to the Investigating Officer; clothes were recovered on the appellant's disclosure statement; concurrent findings warrant no interference
defence_argument: No motive; last seen theory wrongly applied given the long gap between last seen and recovery of body; recovery of clothes not proved in accordance with law; no independent witness examined
legal_principle_applied: Last seen theory applies only where the time gap is small; if a question is not put in cross-examination on an issue, the correctness of that fact cannot later be raised; chain of circumstantial evidence must be complete
precedent_relied_upon: Shankar v. State of Karnataka, AIR 2011 SC 2302; State of Rajasthan v. Rajendra Singh, AIR 1998 SC 2554; State v. Saravanan, AIR 2009 SC 152; Arumugam v. State, AIR 2009 SC 331; Mahendra Pratap Singh v. State of UP, (2009) 11 SCC 334; Vijay alias Chinee v. State of MP, (2010) 8 SCC 191; State of UP v. Naresh, (2011) 4 SCC 324; Brahm Swaroop v. State of UP, AIR 2011 SC 280; Sunil Kumar Sambhudayal Gupta v. State of Maharashtra, (2010) 13 SCC 657; Atluri Brahmanandam v. Anne Sai Bapuji, AIR 2011 SC 545; Laxmibai v. Bhagwantbuva, AIR 2013 SC 1204
